questions.q: How many electoral votes are needed to win the presidency?
questions.note: 270 of 538 — a majority.

questions.q: How many electors are in the Electoral College?
questions.note: 435 House seats, 100 senators, plus 3 for the District of Columbia.

questions.q: How many voting members are in the US House of Representatives?
questions.note: Fixed at 435 by the Permanent Apportionment Act of 1929.

questions.q: How many amendments have been made to the US Constitution?
questions.note: The 27th, on congressional pay, was ratified in 1992 — 202 years after it was proposed.

questions.q: In which year was the Bill of Rights ratified?
questions.note: December 1791.

questions.q: In which year was the US Constitution signed in Philadelphia?
questions.note: 17 September 1787.

questions.q: How many men signed the Declaration of Independence?
questions.note: 56 delegates, most signing on 2 August 1776.

questions.q: How many delegates signed the Constitution at the Constitutional Convention?
questions.note: 39 of the 55 who attended.

questions.q: How many states must ratify a constitutional amendment for it to take effect?
questions.note: Three quarters of the 50 states.

questions.q: How many Senate votes are needed to override a presidential veto?
questions.note: Two thirds of those present and voting — 67 when the full Senate votes.

questions.q: How many justices sit on the Supreme Court?
questions.note: Set by the Judiciary Act of 1869.

questions.q: For how many years did Justice William O. Douglas serve on the Supreme Court?
questions.note: 36 years and 209 days, from 1939 to 1975.

questions.q: How many additional justices did FDR's 1937 court-packing plan propose adding?
questions.note: Up to six, which would have taken the bench to 15. The bill failed.

questions.q: In which year was the 22nd Amendment, limiting presidents to two terms, ratified?
questions.note: 1951, prompted by FDR's four election wins.

questions.q: In which year did the 19th Amendment give women the vote nationwide?
questions.note: Ratified 18 August 1920.

questions.q: In which year did the 26th Amendment lower the voting age to 18?
questions.note: 1971 — ratified in just over three months, the fastest in US history.

questions.q: In which year did the 23rd Amendment give the District of Columbia electoral votes?
questions.note: 1961. DC gets three.

questions.q: In which year was the 13th Amendment, abolishing slavery, ratified?
questions.note: December 1865.

questions.q: In which year was the Civil Rights Act outlawing segregation in public accommodations signed?
questions.note: Signed by Lyndon Johnson on 2 July 1964.

questions.q: In which year was the Voting Rights Act signed into law?
questions.note: 6 August 1965.

questions.q: How many presidential elections did Franklin D. Roosevelt win?
How many bills did Franklin D. Roosevelt veto — more than any other president?
questions.note: 635, of which only nine were overridden.

questions.q: How many US presidents have died in office?
questions.note: Four assassinated, four from natural causes.

questions.q: How many US presidents have been assassinated?
questions.note: Lincoln, Garfield, McKinley and Kennedy.

questions.q: How many times has the House voted to impeach a US president?
questions.note: Four: Andrew Johnson, Bill Clinton, and Donald Trump twice. The Senate convicted none of them.

questions.q: How old was John F. Kennedy when he was inaugurated?
questions.note: 43 — the youngest man ever elected president.

questions.q: How old was Theodore Roosevelt when he became president?
questions.note: 42, the youngest ever to hold the office, after McKinley's assassination.

questions.q: How old was Ronald Reagan at his first inauguration?
questions.note: 69, then the oldest man to take the oath.

questions.q: How many electoral votes did Ronald Reagan win in 1984?
questions.note: 525 of 538 — the largest electoral college total ever.

questions.q: How many states did Ronald Reagan carry in 1984?
questions.note: All but Minnesota, Walter Mondale's home state.

questions.q: How many electoral votes did Richard Nixon win in 1972?
questions.note: 520, carrying 49 states.

questions.q: How many days did the longest US government shutdown last?
questions.note: 43 days, from 1 October to 12 November 2025, breaking the 35-day record set in 2018-19.

questions.q: How many hours did Strom Thurmond speak in his 1957 filibuster?
questions.note: 24 hours and 18 minutes, against the Civil Rights Act of 1957.

questions.q: How many executive departments are there in the federal government?
questions.note: Fifteen, from State, the oldest, to Homeland Security, created in 2002.

questions.q: What is the annual salary of the US president, in dollars?
questions.note: $400,000, set in 2001. It was $200,000 for the three decades before that.

questions.q: In which year was the Federal Reserve created?
questions.note: The Federal Reserve Act was signed in December 1913.

questions.q: How many rooms are there in the White House?
questions.note: 132 rooms, including 35 bathrooms.

questions.q: In which year did a president first live in the White House?
questions.note: John Adams moved in during November 1800.

questions.q: In which year did Alaska become a state?
questions.note: 3 January 1959, the 49th state.

questions.q: In which year did Hawaii become a state?
questions.note: 21 August 1959, the 50th state.

questions.q: In which year did national Prohibition take effect?
questions.note: January 1920, under the 18th Amendment.

questions.q: In which year was Prohibition repealed?
questions.note: The 21st Amendment, December 1933.

questions.q: In which year was Ronald Reagan shot outside the Washington Hilton?
questions.note: 30 March 1981, 69 days into his presidency.

questions.q: How many years is a full term for a US senator?
questions.note: Six, with a third of the Senate up for election every two years.

questions.q: How many votes were cast for president in the 2020 election, in millions?
questions.note: About 158.4 million votes for president, the highest raw total in US history.

questions.q: What percentage of eligible voters turned out in the 2020 presidential election?
questions.note: About 66.8%, the highest rate since 1900.

questions.q: How many electoral votes did California have in the 2024 election?
questions.note: 54 — the largest of any state.

questions.q: How many electoral votes does Wyoming have — the minimum any state can hold?
questions.note: Three: one for each senator and one for its single House seat.

questions.q: John Marshall was the longest-serving Chief Justice. How many years did he lead the Court?
questions.note: 34 years, from 1801 to 1835.

questions.q: In which year did the first US Congress convene?
questions.note: March 1789, in New York City.

questions.q: How many original colonies formed the United States?
questions.note: Thirteen, from New Hampshire to Georgia.

questions.q: In which year was Jamestown founded?
questions.note: 1607 — the first permanent English settlement in America.

questions.q: In which year did the Mayflower reach Cape Cod?
questions.note: November 1620, after 66 days at sea.

questions.q: How many passengers sailed on the Mayflower?
questions.note: 102 passengers and roughly 30 crew.

questions.q: In which year did the Salem witch trials take place?
questions.note: 1692, in colonial Massachusetts.

questions.q: How many people were executed in the Salem witch trials?
questions.note: Nineteen hanged and one pressed to death.

questions.q: In which year was the Boston Tea Party?
questions.note: 16 December 1773.

questions.q: How many chests of tea were thrown into Boston Harbor?
questions.note: 342 chests, worth about £10,000 at the time.

questions.q: In which year did Paul Revere make his midnight ride?
questions.note: 18 April 1775, the night before Lexington and Concord.

questions.q: In which year was the Declaration of Independence adopted?
questions.note: 4 July 1776.

questions.q: In which year did Cornwallis surrender at Yorktown?
questions.note: October 1781, effectively ending the fighting.

questions.q: In which year did the Treaty of Paris formally end the Revolutionary War?
questions.note: September 1783.

questions.q: In which year was the Louisiana Purchase agreed?
questions.note: 1803, doubling the size of the country.

questions.q: How much did the United States pay for the Louisiana Purchase, in millions of dollars?
questions.note: $15 million — roughly three cents an acre.

questions.q: In which year did Lewis and Clark first reach the Pacific Ocean?
questions.note: November 1805, after 18 months on the trail.

questions.q: How much did the United States pay Russia for Alaska, in millions of dollars?
questions.note: $7.2 million in 1867 — about two cents an acre.

questions.q: In which year did Texas join the Union?
questions.note: December 1845, as the 28th state.

questions.q: In which year was gold discovered at Sutter's Mill?
questions.note: January 1848, touching off the California Gold Rush.

questions.q: In which year did the Erie Canal open?
questions.note: 1825, linking the Hudson River to the Great Lakes.

questions.q: How long is the Erie Canal, in miles?
questions.note: 363 miles from Albany to Buffalo.

questions.q: How many months did the Pony Express operate?
questions.note: Just 18 months — the telegraph put it out of business.

questions.q: In which year did the 'Great Migration' wagon train set out on the Oregon Trail?
questions.note: 1843, when about 1,000 settlers made the crossing in a single train.

questions.q: In which year did the Cherokee removal known as the Trail of Tears begin?
questions.note: 1838. Thousands died on the march west to Indian Territory.

questions.q: How many days did the siege of the Alamo last?
questions.note: Thirteen days, ending on 6 March 1836.

questions.q: In which year did the Civil War begin at Fort Sumter?
questions.note: April 1861.

questions.q: How many states seceded to form the Confederacy?
questions.note: Eleven seceded, though the Confederate flag carried 13 stars.

questions.q: In which year was the transcontinental railroad completed at Promontory Summit?
questions.note: 10 May 1869, with a golden spike.

questions.q: In which year was the Wounded Knee massacre?
questions.note: December 1890.

questions.q: In which year was the Statue of Liberty dedicated?
questions.note: 28 October 1886, a gift from France.

questions.q: How tall is the Statue of Liberty from ground to torch, in feet?
questions.note: 305 feet including the pedestal; the statue alone is 151 feet.

questions.q: In which year was the Brooklyn Bridge completed?
questions.note: 1883 — the longest suspension bridge in the world at the time.

questions.q: In which year did Ellis Island open as an immigration station?
questions.note: 1892. It processed arrivals until 1954.

questions.q: How many immigrants passed through Ellis Island, in millions?
questions.note: About 12 million over 62 years.

questions.q: In which year did the Wright brothers make their first powered flight?
questions.note: 17 December 1903, at Kitty Hawk.

questions.q: How long was the Wright brothers' first flight, in feet?
questions.note: 120 feet in 12 seconds.

questions.q: In which year was the Ford Model T introduced?
questions.note: 1908. Fifteen million were built.

questions.q: What did the cheapest Ford Model T body style cost in 1925, in dollars?
questions.note: $260 for the Runabout — down from $850 at launch.

questions.q: In which year did the Panama Canal open?
questions.note: August 1914, after a decade of American construction.

questions.q: In which year did the Wall Street Crash begin?
questions.note: October 1929.

questions.q: What was the peak unemployment rate during the Great Depression?
questions.note: About 25% in 1933.

questions.q: In which year did the Empire State Building open?
questions.note: 1931, built in just 410 days.

questions.q: How tall is the Empire State Building to the tip, in feet?
questions.note: 1,454 feet including the spire; 1,250 feet to the roof.

questions.q: In which year did President Roosevelt dedicate the Hoover Dam?
questions.note: September 1935. The last concrete had been poured that May.

questions.q: In which year did the Golden Gate Bridge open?
How long is the Golden Gate Bridge's main span, in feet?
questions.note: 4,200 feet — the longest suspension span in the world until 1964.

questions.q: In which year was Route 66 established?
questions.note: 1926, running Chicago to Santa Monica.

questions.q: How long was Route 66, in miles?
questions.note: 2,448 miles across eight states.

questions.q: In which year did construction of the Interstate Highway System begin?
questions.note: 1956, under the Federal-Aid Highway Act.

questions.q: In which year did Ford introduce the moving assembly line?
questions.note: 1913 at Highland Park. It cut Model T assembly from 12 hours to about 90 minutes.

questions.q: How tall is the Washington Monument, in feet?
questions.note: 555 feet — the tallest structure in the world when finished in 1884.

questions.q: In which year was Pearl Harbor attacked?
questions.note: 7 December 1941.

questions.q: How many Americans were killed at Pearl Harbor?
questions.note: 2,403 dead, nearly half of them aboard the USS Arizona.

questions.q: How many men died aboard the USS Arizona at Pearl Harbor?
questions.note: 1,177 — most still entombed in the wreck.

questions.q: In which year did the D-Day landings take place?
questions.note: 6 June 1944.

questions.q: About how many Allied troops landed in Normandy on D-Day, by sea and air?
questions.note: About 156,000. Estimates vary; roughly 132,000 came by sea and the rest by air.

questions.q: According to the Department of Veterans Affairs, how many Americans in uniform died in the Second World War?
questions.note: 405,399 — 291,557 in battle and 113,842 from other causes.

questions.q: How many American service members died in the First World War?
questions.note: 116,516, over half from disease.

questions.q: In which year was the Korean War armistice signed?
questions.note: 27 July 1953, at Panmunjom. No peace treaty has ever followed.

questions.q: How many American service members died in the Vietnam War?
questions.note: 58,220 US military deaths. The Wall in Washington carries 58,281 names.

questions.q: How many US troops were in Vietnam at the peak in 1969?
questions.note: About 543,000 in April 1969.

questions.q: How many days did the Battle of the Bulge last?
questions.note: 16 December 1944 to 25 January 1945.

questions.q: How many days did the Battle of Iwo Jima last?
questions.note: 36 days of fighting in early 1945.

questions.q: How many Americans were killed at Iwo Jima?
questions.note: 6,821 killed and nearly 20,000 wounded.

questions.q: In which year was the Battle of Midway?
questions.note: June 1942, the turning point in the Pacific.

questions.q: How many Japanese aircraft carriers were sunk at Midway?
questions.note: Four of the six carriers that had struck Pearl Harbor were sunk in a single day.

questions.q: How many casualties were suffered at Antietam, the bloodiest single day in American history?
questions.note: About 22,700 killed, wounded or missing on 17 September 1862.

questions.q: In which year was the Battle of Gettysburg?
How many casualties were suffered at Gettysburg over three days?
questions.note: About 51,000 across both armies.

questions.q: In which year was the Battle of the Little Bighorn?
How many men of the 7th Cavalry were killed at the Little Bighorn?
questions.note: 268 killed across the regiment; Custer's own battalion of about 210 was wiped out.

questions.q: How many Continental soldiers encamped at Valley Forge?
questions.note: About 12,000. Roughly 2,000 died over the winter of 1777–78.

questions.q: In which year was the USS Constitution launched?
questions.note: 1797. She is still a commissioned Navy ship.

questions.q: In which year was the US Marine Corps founded?
questions.note: 10 November 1775, at Tun Tavern in Philadelphia.

questions.q: In which year was West Point established as a military academy?
questions.note: 1802, under Thomas Jefferson.

questions.q: In which year was the US Naval Academy founded at Annapolis?
In which year was the Pentagon completed?
questions.note: January 1943, after just 16 months of construction.

questions.q: How many miles of corridors are inside the Pentagon?
questions.note: 17.5 miles, yet no two points are more than a seven-minute walk apart.

questions.q: How many Medals of Honor were awarded for the Second World War?
questions.note: 472, well over half of them posthumously.

questions.q: How many Medals of Honor were awarded for the Civil War?
questions.note: 1,523 — by far the most of any conflict.

questions.q: What did the Manhattan Project cost, in billions of 1945 dollars?
questions.note: About $2 billion, roughly $30 billion today.

questions.q: What was the yield of the Hiroshima bomb, in kilotons?
questions.note: About 15 kilotons of TNT equivalent.

questions.q: How many days did the Berlin Airlift last?
questions.note: 462 days, from 26 June 1948 to 30 September 1949, delivering over two million tons of supplies.

questions.q: How many hours did the Desert Storm ground war last?
questions.note: 100 hours before the ceasefire.

questions.q: In which year did Operation Desert Storm begin?
questions.note: January 1991. The wider Gulf War had begun with Iraq's invasion of Kuwait in August 1990.

questions.q: How many B-17 Flying Fortresses were built?
questions.note: 12,731 between 1936 and 1945.

questions.q: How many crew flew in a B-17 Flying Fortress?
questions.note: Ten men manning thirteen .50 calibre machine guns.

questions.q: How many P-51 Mustangs were built?
How many M4 Sherman tanks were built?
questions.note: 49,234 — the most-produced American tank of the war.

questions.q: How many Liberty ships were built during the Second World War?
questions.note: 2,710. At the peak, one was launched roughly every day.

questions.q: What was the SR-71 Blackbird's official top speed, in mph?
questions.note: 2,193 mph — a record it still holds for a manned air-breathing aircraft.

questions.q: What is the U-2's service ceiling, in feet?
questions.note: Above 70,000 feet, at the edge of space.

questions.q: What is the B-52's unrefuelled range, in miles?
questions.note: About 8,800 miles.

questions.q: In which year did the B-52 enter service?
questions.note: 1955 — and it is expected to fly into the 2050s.

questions.q: According to the US Air Force, what does a B-2 Spirit cost, in millions of 1998 dollars?
questions.note: $1.157 billion apiece in constant 1998 dollars. Counting development, the programme average was nearer $2 billion.

questions.q: How many B-2 Spirit bombers were built?
questions.note: 21, of which one was lost in a crash in 2008.

questions.q: How long is a Nimitz-class aircraft carrier, in feet?
questions.note: 1,092 feet — nearly a quarter of a mile.

questions.q: In which year was the USS Nimitz commissioned?
questions.note: 1975. She was still serving half a century later.

questions.q: How much does an M1A2 SEPv3 Abrams weigh, in short tons?
questions.note: 73.6 short tons — the tank has gained over ten tons since the original M1.

questions.q: What is the F-16's top speed, in mph?
questions.note: About 1,500 mph — Mach 2 at altitude, per the USAF fact sheet.

questions.q: In which year was the first production F-16 delivered to the US Air Force?
questions.note: August 1978. The first operational wing stood up the following January.

questions.q: How many teams are in the NFL?
questions.note: 32, split evenly between the AFC and NFC.

questions.q: How many games are in an NFL regular season?
questions.note: 17 since 2021, up from 16.

questions.q: How many players are on an NFL active roster?
questions.note: 53 on the roster, with 48 active on game day.

questions.q: In which year was the NFL founded?
questions.note: 1920, as the American Professional Football Association.

questions.q: In which year was the AFL-NFL merger completed?
questions.note: 1970, creating the AFC and NFC.

questions.q: In which year was the first Super Bowl played?
questions.note: January 1967, Packers over Chiefs.

questions.q: How long is a football field including both end zones, in yards?
questions.note: 100 yards of playing field plus two 10-yard end zones.

questions.q: How wide is an NFL field, in feet?
questions.note: 160 feet, or 53⅓ yards.

questions.q: How high is the crossbar on an NFL goalpost, in feet?
questions.note: Ten feet above the ground.

questions.q: How far apart are NFL goalpost uprights, in feet?
questions.note: 18 feet 6 inches — college posts are wider.

questions.q: How many seconds are on the NFL play clock?
questions.note: 40 seconds from the end of the previous play.

questions.q: How many minutes are in an NFL quarter?
questions.note: Fifteen, for 60 minutes of game clock.

questions.q: How many officials are on an NFL officiating crew?
questions.note: Seven, led by the referee.

questions.q: What is the maximum weight of an NFL football, in ounces?
questions.note: The rulebook allows 14 to 15 ounces.

questions.q: How many teams make the NFL playoffs?
questions.note: Fourteen — seven from each conference.

questions.q: How many rounds are in the NFL draft?
questions.note: Seven, down from 12 as recently as 1992.

questions.q: How many Super Bowls did Tom Brady win?
questions.note: Seven — more than any single franchise.

questions.q: How many regular-season passing yards did Tom Brady finish his career with?
questions.note: 89,214 in the regular season, the all-time record.

questions.q: How many regular-season touchdown passes did Tom Brady throw?
questions.note: 649 in the regular season.

questions.q: How many Super Bowl MVP awards did Tom Brady win?
questions.note: Five, the most by any player.

questions.q: How many Super Bowls have the New England Patriots won?
questions.note: Six, all with Brady and Belichick.

questions.q: How many Super Bowls have the Pittsburgh Steelers won?
questions.note: Six, tied for the most in NFL history.

questions.q: How many Super Bowls have the Dallas Cowboys won?
questions.note: Five, the last in the 1995 season.

questions.q: How many Super Bowls have the Patriots appeared in?
questions.note: Twelve — the most of any franchise, after losing Super Bowl LX in February 2026.

questions.q: How many regular-season rushing yards did Emmitt Smith finish his career with?
questions.note: 18,355 — still the NFL record.

questions.q: How many regular-season rushing touchdowns did Emmitt Smith score?
questions.note: 164, the all-time record.

questions.q: How many regular-season receiving yards did Jerry Rice finish his career with?
questions.note: 22,895 — more than 5,400 clear of Larry Fitzgerald in second.

questions.q: How many regular-season receptions did Jerry Rice finish his career with?
How many regular-season receiving touchdowns did Jerry Rice score?
questions.note: 197, and 208 touchdowns in total.

questions.q: How many regular-season sacks did Bruce Smith record?
questions.note: 200 exactly — the all-time record.

questions.q: How many regular-season points did Adam Vinatieri score, the most in NFL history?
questions.note: 2,673 over 24 seasons.

questions.q: How many consecutive regular-season starts did Brett Favre make?
questions.note: 297 — 321 including the playoffs.

questions.q: How many passing yards did Dan Marino throw for in 1984?
questions.note: 5,084 — a record that stood for 27 years.

questions.q: How many touchdown passes did Peyton Manning throw in 2013?
questions.note: 55, the single-season record.

questions.q: How many rushing yards did Eric Dickerson gain in 1984?
questions.note: 2,105, still the single-season record.

questions.q: How many rushing yards did Adrian Peterson gain in a single game in 2007?
questions.note: 296 against the Chargers — the single-game record.

questions.q: How long is the longest field goal in NFL history, in yards?
questions.note: 68 yards, by Cam Little of Jacksonville in November 2025.

questions.q: What is the most points scored by one team in an NFL game?
questions.note: 72, by Washington against the Giants in 1966.

questions.q: To the nearest minute, how many minutes of playing time did the longest NFL game last?
questions.note: 82 minutes 40 seconds — Dolphins beat Chiefs on Christmas Day 1971.

questions.q: How many games did the undefeated 1972 Miami Dolphins win, including the playoffs?
questions.note: 17–0, the only perfect season in NFL history.

questions.q: How many regular-season games did the 1985 Chicago Bears win?
questions.note: 15–1, losing only to Miami.

questions.q: How tall is the Vince Lombardi Trophy, in inches?
questions.note: 22 inches of sterling silver, made by Tiffany & Co.

questions.q: How much does the Vince Lombardi Trophy weigh, in pounds?
questions.note: About seven pounds.

questions.q: In which year was the forward pass legalized in American football?
questions.note: 1906, to make the game less lethal.

questions.q: What is the standard seating capacity of AT&T Stadium, home of the Cowboys?
questions.note: About 80,000, expandable past 100,000.

questions.q: What is the fastest 40-yard dash ever recorded at the NFL Combine, in seconds?
questions.note: 4.21 by Xavier Worthy in 2024.

questions.q: What did a 30-second Super Bowl advert cost in 2024, in millions of dollars?
questions.note: About $7 million.

questions.q: In which year was the trophy now known as the Heisman first awarded?
questions.note: 1935, to Jay Berwanger. It was called the DAC Trophy until Heisman died the following year.

questions.q: In which year was the first Rose Bowl game played?
questions.note: 1902, making it the oldest bowl game.

questions.q: How many minutes long is an NFL regular-season overtime period?
questions.note: Ten minutes, reduced from 15 in 2017.

questions.q: In which year was the Second Amendment ratified?
questions.note: 1791, as part of the Bill of Rights.

questions.q: How many words are in the Second Amendment?
questions.note: 27 words, and lawyers have argued about the commas ever since.

questions.q: In which year was the National Firearms Act passed?
questions.note: 1934, taxing and registering machine guns and short-barrelled weapons.

questions.q: In which year was the Gun Control Act passed?
In which year was District of Columbia v. Heller decided?
questions.note: 2008 — the Court's first ruling squarely on the individual right.

questions.q: In which year did the Brady Handgun Violence Prevention Act take effect?
questions.note: February 1994, creating the waiting period that became NICS.

questions.q: In which year was Colt's Patent Fire-Arms Manufacturing Company founded?
questions.note: 1855 in Hartford, Connecticut.

questions.q: In which year did Smith & Wesson begin operations in Springfield, Massachusetts?
questions.note: 1856. An earlier 1852 partnership became Volcanic Repeating Arms.

questions.q: In which year was Remington founded?
questions.note: 1816 — the oldest American gunmaker, though the business passed through bankruptcy in 2020.

questions.q: In which year was the Winchester Repeating Arms Company founded?
questions.note: 1866, out of the old New Haven Arms Company.

questions.q: In which year was Sturm, Ruger & Co. founded?
questions.note: 1949, in a rented machine shop.

questions.q: In which year was the Colt Single Action Army introduced?
questions.note: 1873 — 'the gun that won the West'.

questions.q: How many first-generation Colt Single Action Army revolvers were produced?
In which year was the Henry rifle introduced?
questions.note: 1860. Confederates called it 'that damned Yankee rifle you load on Sunday and shoot all week'.

questions.q: How many rounds did the original Henry rifle's magazine hold?
questions.note: Fifteen in the magazine, sixteen with one in the chamber.

questions.q: In which year was the Winchester Model 1894 introduced?
questions.note: 1894, designed by John Browning.

questions.q: In which year did US production of the Winchester Model 1894 end?
questions.note: March 2006, when the New Haven plant closed after 112 years.

questions.q: In which year was the Gatling gun patented?
questions.note: 1862, by Richard Gatling.

questions.q: What was the rate of fire of the original Gatling gun, in rounds per minute?
questions.note: About 200 rounds per minute by hand crank.

questions.q: In which year was the Springfield M1903 rifle adopted?
questions.note: 1903, and it stayed in service through the Second World War.

questions.q: In which year was the M1911 pistol adopted by the US Army?
questions.note: 1911, designed by John Browning.

questions.q: How many rounds does a standard M1911 magazine hold?
questions.note: Seven rounds of .45 ACP.

questions.q: In which year did the Beretta M9 replace the M1911 as the US service pistol?
How many rounds does a standard Beretta M9 magazine hold?
questions.note: Fifteen rounds of 9mm.

questions.q: In which year was the M1 Garand adopted?
questions.note: 1936. Patton called it 'the greatest battle implement ever devised'.

questions.q: How many rounds are in an M1 Garand en bloc clip?
questions.note: Eight — and the clip ejects with an audible ping.

questions.q: How much does an M1 Garand weigh, in pounds?
questions.note: About 9.5 pounds unloaded.

questions.q: How many M1 Garands were produced in total between 1937 and 1957, in millions?
questions.note: About 5,468,000 in total.

questions.q: In which year did the Thompson submachine gun enter production?
questions.note: 1921. The Army bought it, but Prohibition made it famous.

questions.q: What is the rate of fire of the M1921 Thompson, in rounds per minute?
questions.note: About 800 rounds per minute. Later M1928 and M1 variants were slowed to around 600.

questions.q: In which year was the M2 Browning heavy machine gun adopted?
questions.note: 1933 — and it is still in front-line service.

questions.q: How much does an M2 Browning machine gun weigh without its tripod, in pounds?
questions.note: 84 pounds for the M2HB — the tripod adds another 44.

questions.q: What is the M2 Browning's effective range, in yards?
questions.note: About 2,000 yards.

questions.q: How much does the M1918 Browning Automatic Rifle weigh, in pounds?
questions.note: About 16 pounds — the reason BAR men were chosen for their size.

questions.q: In which year did ArmaLite sell the AR-15 design to Colt?
questions.note: 1959. ArmaLite had developed the rifle from 1956.

questions.q: In which year was the M16A1 standardized as the US Army's service rifle?
questions.note: 1967. The Air Force had adopted an earlier version in 1964.

questions.q: How much does an M16A2 weigh without magazine or sling, in pounds?
questions.note: 7.78 pounds per the Army field manual; 8.79 pounds with a loaded 30-round magazine.

questions.q: How many rounds does a standard AR-15 magazine hold?
questions.note: Thirty, though 20-round magazines came first.

questions.q: What is the muzzle velocity of 5.56mm M193 ball from a 20-inch barrel, in feet per second?
questions.note: About 3,250 fps. From a 14.5-inch M4 barrel the same round drops to roughly 3,000.

questions.q: What is the published muzzle velocity of a commercial 150-grain .30-06 load, in feet per second?
questions.note: About 2,910 fps. Military M2 ball ran nearer 2,740 fps.

questions.q: What is the muzzle energy of a 150-grain .308 Winchester load, in foot-pounds?
questions.note: About 2,650 foot-pounds.

questions.q: What is the typical muzzle velocity of a high-velocity .22 Long Rifle round, in feet per second?
questions.note: Around 1,250 fps. Standard-velocity loads run closer to 1,120.

questions.q: What is the muzzle velocity of a .50 BMG round, in feet per second?
questions.note: About 2,900 fps.

questions.q: In which year was the AK-47 adopted by the Soviet Army?
How old was Mikhail Kalashnikov when he died in 2013?
questions.note: 94. Late in life he said he wished he had invented a lawnmower instead.

questions.q: What is the muzzle velocity of a 7.62x39mm round, in feet per second?
questions.note: About 2,350 fps.

questions.q: In which year was the Glock 17 introduced?
questions.note: 1982, when it won the Austrian army pistol contract.

questions.q: How many rounds does a standard Glock 17 magazine hold?
questions.note: Seventeen rounds of 9mm in the standard magazine.

questions.q: In which year did Remington build its 10 millionth Model 870 shotgun?
questions.note: April 2009 — the best-selling shotgun ever made.

questions.q: In which year was the Ruger 10/22 introduced?
questions.note: 1964, and it has been in continuous production ever since.
